sources.title: Replenishment
sources.scope: Fetched official Retail Merchandising Foundation Cloud replenishment overview.
supported_claims: Replenishment refills stores or warehouses from a supplier or warehouse.
The process can generate recommendations for manual review rather than automatically create orders or transfers.
Item/location inventory, forecast integration and rounding/constraints are relevant planning concepts.
sources.limitations: Unversioned latest page; no installed Oracle version or connection is asserted. Does not define this sample DC-case budget, lost-demand model, ceiling or allocation queue.

sources.title: Replenishment methods and quantity modification
sources.scope: Fetched official Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management coverage codes and order quantity multiple sections.
supported_claims: Replenishment planning can use period, requirement, minimum-maximum and manual methods.
Planned orders can be constrained to multiples of a configured quantity.
sources.limitations: Microsoft's minimum-maximum examples can select a lower multiple before overshoot. This scenario's unconditional case ceiling is explicitly different sample policy, not engine parity.

sources.title: Overview of the Forecast to plan business process areas
sources.scope: Fetched official stocking/replenishment policies, forecast supply and demand, and plan supply and replenishment sections.
supported_claims: Stocking policies include replenishment lead times, inventory thresholds and planning horizons.
Expected demand, safety stock, inventory and capacity considerations inform replenishment planning.
sources.limitations: Cross-product process guidance, not an exact store/DC allocation formula, a mandate for case-count capacity, or a live inventory accuracy guarantee.
